transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm really only here because my wife and family insisted on it. I just can’t shake this constant fear of putting on weight, so I keep cutting back on what I eat, even though everyone at home says I’m already too thin.
Do you ever feel like you lose control over your eating and consume a very large amount of food in a short period of time?

No, I never lose control like that; it's actually the exact opposite. I keep extremely rigid control over everything I eat, often just skipping meals or pushing tiny portions of food around my plate. The mere thought of eating a normal meal or a second helping completely panics me.
How has your physical health been affected by your eating habits, specifically regarding your menstrual cycle or any feelings of dizziness and fatigue?

Well, I'm a man, so I don't have a menstrual cycle, but I have been feeling pretty drained, cold, and lightheaded lately, and I even passed out once at the auto shop. Honestly, though, I think everyone is overreacting to that—it's just a minor side effect of me being disciplined about my health.
When you look at yourself in the mirror, do you see yourself as being too thin, or do you still perceive areas of your body as being overweight?

When I look in the mirror, I don't see myself as "too thin" at all, despite what my family and the doctors say. Honestly, I feel a sense of pride seeing how lean and "shredded" I've gotten, because to me it just shows my discipline. But I still have this constant worry that if I let my guard down, I'll lose that definition and immediately start putting on weight.
